pr_title: demo: docs review target — exporter without docstrings

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Exporter class
findings.explanation: The Exporter class is uncovered as a whole, meaning its integrated behavior across supported export methods is not exercised by tests.
findings.suggestion: Add class-level tests for Exporter that exercise construction and each supported export path with representative note data, including empty-note and multi-note cases.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Exporter.__init__
findings.explanation: Exporter.__init__ is uncovered by tests, so initialization behavior and stored state are not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test that constructs an Exporter with representative notes and verifies the instance stores the provided data/configuration correctly.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Exporter.to_json
findings.explanation: Exporter.to_json is uncovered by tests, so JSON export formatting and serialization behavior are not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for Exporter.to_json that exports sample notes and asserts the returned JSON is valid and contains the expected fields and values.

findings.title: JSON export may fail on non-JSON-serializable timestamps
findings.explanation: The JSON exporter passes `n.created_at` directly to `json.dumps`. If `Note.created_at` is a `datetime`/`date` object, which the field name strongly suggests, JSON export will fail at runtime with `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, while the CSV and Markdown exporters implicitly stringify it.
findings.suggestion: Normalize exported values before serializing, e.g. use `n.created_at.isoformat()` for datetime-like values, or centralize note-to-primitive conversion in a helper used by all formats.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Exporter.to_csv
findings.explanation: Exporter.to_csv is uncovered by tests, so CSV output formatting, headers, and escaping behavior are not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for Exporter.to_csv using sample notes, including values that require CSV escaping, and assert the header row and data rows are correct.

findings.title: CSV formula injection in exported notes
findings.explanation: User-controlled note content is written directly into CSV cells. If a note text begins with characters interpreted as a spreadsheet formula, such as `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab, or carriage return, opening the exported CSV in Excel/LibreOffice/Google Sheets can execute attacker-supplied formulas, potentially leading to data exfiltration or command execution in vulnerable spreadsheet configurations. CSV quoting does not prevent spreadsheet formula interpretation.
findings.suggestion: Before writing untrusted strings to CSV, neutralize spreadsheet formulas. For example, wrap CSV output values with a sanitizer that prefixes a single quote to any string whose first character is one of `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, `\t`, or `\r`, and apply it to all string fields, including `n.text` and any other fields that may become user-controlled. Alternatively, export with a format not opened by spreadsheets, or document and enforce safe consumers.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Exporter.to_markdown
findings.explanation: Exporter.to_markdown is uncovered by tests, so Markdown output structure and content are not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for Exporter.to_markdown that exports representative notes and asserts the Markdown contains the expected headings, note content, and formatting.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Exporter.write
findings.explanation: Exporter.write is uncovered by tests, so writing exported content to disk and handling different formats are not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for Exporter.write using a temporary path to verify it writes the expected content for supported export formats and handles unsupported formats as intended.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for export_all
findings.explanation: export_all is uncovered by tests, so the top-level export orchestration behavior is not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for export_all that supplies sample notes and a temporary output location, then asserts all expected export files or outputs are produced correctly.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for summarize_for_export
findings.explanation: summarize_for_export is uncovered by tests, so export summary generation is not verified.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for summarize_for_export with representative notes and assert the returned summary includes the expected counts, titles, tags, or other summary fields.

findings.title: Missing docstring for Exporter
findings.explanation: Public class `Exporter` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Export notes to supported output formats."

findings.title: Missing docstring for Exporter.to_json
findings.explanation: Public method `Exporter.to_json` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Return the exported notes as a JSON string."

findings.title: Missing docstring for Exporter.to_csv
findings.explanation: Public method `Exporter.to_csv` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Return the exported notes as CSV-formatted text."

findings.title: Missing docstring for Exporter.to_markdown
findings.explanation: Public method `Exporter.to_markdown` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Return the exported notes as Markdown-formatted text."

findings.title: Unescaped note text in Markdown export may lead to downstream XSS
findings.explanation: Raw note text is inserted into Markdown without escaping. Many Markdown renderers allow embedded HTML or dangerous links, so if this export is later rendered to HTML in a web context, a malicious note could become stored cross-site scripting or content injection.
findings.suggestion: If Markdown exports may be rendered in a browser, either escape or sanitize note text before including it, configure the Markdown renderer to disable raw HTML and dangerous URL schemes, and sanitize the generated HTML with an allowlist-based sanitizer such as Bleach. If the export is strictly plain text and never rendered as HTML, document that assumption.

findings.title: Stringly typed export format dispatch is hard to extend
findings.explanation: `write` uses open-ended string values and a growing `if`/`elif` dispatch chain for formats. This makes supported formats less discoverable, allows typos until runtime, and requires editing branching logic every time a format is added.
findings.suggestion: Define supported formats in one place, for example `Literal['json', 'csv', 'markdown']` for the parameter and/or a mapping like `{'json': self.to_json, ...}`. This keeps dispatch data-driven and makes the valid values explicit.

findings.title: Missing docstring for Exporter.write
findings.explanation: Public method `Exporter.write` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Write the exported notes to the given path using the specified format."

findings.title: Missing docstring for export_all
findings.explanation: Public function `export_all` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Export all notes to the given path using the specified format."

findings.title: Missing docstring for summarize_for_export
findings.explanation: Public function `summarize_for_export` is missing a docstring.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line docstring such as: "Return a summary of notes prepared for export."

summary: The PR has medium-severity security and quality issues in export handling, notably CSV formula injection and potential JSON timestamp serialization failures. Test coverage for the new export module is also broadly missing.
